stem.en: Kabir says: "Franklin only had a blurry X. She could have been wrong about the helix." What made the X convincing?

text.en: An X pattern is what a helix, and only a helix, casts. The spacings in the X gave exact numbers for the turn and the rungs, and a model built to those numbers cast the same X back.

feedback.en: The pattern was reproduced many times, and every feature of it matched a helix and nothing else.

text.en: Somebody had seen the helix with a microscope.

feedback.en: No microscope of the time could see a molecule. The helix was inferred, and the inference held.

text.en: The name "double helix" made it true.

feedback.en: The name came after the numbers. Before Photo 51, several shapes were on the table, including a triple helix that the X ruled out.

explanation.en: A good inference makes a prediction. The double helix predicted the exact X, and got it.
